quizData.question: With `box-sizing: border-box; width: 300px; padding: 10px; border: 5px;`, what is the content width?
quizData.explanation: Total width 300px minus padding (20) minus border (10) = 270px content width.

slides.title: When to Use `content-box`? 🔍
slides.content:
# Rare Cases

The default `content-box` is useful when you want the padding/border to be purely additive, e.g., for decorative effects or when you need the content to remain a fixed size.

But for general layout, `border-box` is the standard. You can always apply it globally and then override for specific elements if needed.

quizData.question: Using `box-sizing: border-box;` on the `*` selector will affect pseudo‑elements like `::before`.
quizData.explanation: The universal selector `*` does not apply to pseudo‑elements; you must explicitly include `*::before, *::after` as shown.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Debugging the Box Model

In DevTools, you can toggle `box-sizing` on the fly to see the difference. It's a great way to understand why an element is larger than expected.
